runners_data.name: Melek Alreeh
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse dropping back from 12-14f, with six similar-going runs producing no wins from the front and best form when produced late; 44 days off is not a concern for Simcock, but this pace shape may not generate enough tempo to deliver a winning run from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Melek Alreeh won two starts back and was runner-up three starts back, giving him a lively recent profile, and he has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; 44 days between runs is the one query, but 142 lb from stall four keeps connections' faith.

runners_data.name: Raulin
runners_data.note: Won last time at 12f on good ground and boasts strong similar-going form (11/15, 4W7P) making this the most credible threat from a genuine hold-up position; 68 days since last run is worth monitoring, and a tongue-tie adds a small unknown, but class and style fit the closing role if the gallop quickens.
runners_data.comment: Raulin arrives here as a winner last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him a solid profile at the head of our ratings; the main risk is a 68-day absence.

runners_data.name: Just An Hour
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who will be comfortable tracking Tai Hang Pegasus in second or third, and his consistent placed record over 10-12f on good ground (sim-going 11/15) suits a steady-pace-to-quicken shape; 14 days since last run is fine for Millman, and the drop from 14f back to this trip could release some fresh speed.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and threatening, Just An Hour has finished third three times in his last four starts, arriving here fit on a 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here who will control the race from the front on a track that suits a lone pace-setter; however, a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 signals this is not its optimal tactical scenario, its OR of 78 is modest, and at age 3 in a field of older rivals its ability to sustain the lead to the line is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and his speed rating leaves plenty to find, Tai Hang Pegasus does at least come into this on the back of a win and has experience of today's distance and going, but he is hard to fancy at these weights from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Andrew Balding, and this horse's sim-going record of 8/8 on good ground is the most compelling statistic in the race; a prominent, stalking style suits this pace shape ideally, and his consistent placed and winning form over 10-12f on good gives him clear profile fit for the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Cape Fear has been knocking on the door in recent starts — third two runs back before a runner-up finish last time out — and he has experience of today's distance and going, but he carries 126 lb from stall one and ranks fifth of seven on our assessment.

runners_data.name: Percival
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's runner arrives 23 days fresh and showed a win on heavy at Haydock, but its true racing style is hold-up, placed here in midfield only because the map cannot accommodate more closers; sim-going form of 2/5 on good-to-firm is limited, and racing out of its natural position reduces its chance considerably.
runners_data.comment: Percival shaped with promise when third two starts back and returns in good order after 23 days, with experience of today's going an asset at 140 lb from stall two; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Morcar
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's six-year-old has strong overall form (sim-going 14/15, 2W8P) and experience, but those wins have come at 10f rather than this extended trip, and his natural hold-up style places him in midfield by redistribution rather than design; blinkers are applied but may not overcome the tactical disadvantage of being a closer in a race without a strong enough pace.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out dampens enthusiasm considerably, and with his trainer striking at just 4% recently, Morcar is hard to fancy at these weights, despite winning three starts back and having experience of today's trip and conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Tai Hang Pegasus is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, will dictate from the flag at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m3½f at Windsor. Just An Hour and Cape Fear will track closely in the prominent positions, meaning the front three are relatively well-defined, but the field's hold-up contingent is heavy — Melek Alreeh and Raulin are genuine closers, while Percival and Morcar are natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions because they cannot all operate from the rear in a race this small. The uncontested pace Tai Hang Pegasus sets on fast ground creates a moderate tempo that is unlikely to stretch the field, favouring those who can track and pounce rather than those making up wide margins late. This race shape is tailor-made for prominent-to-close runners who can sit within striking distance of a controlled pace and produce a sustained finish, with genuine hold-up horses likely disadvantaged by the absence of a searching gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus sets a steady uncontested gallop and Cape Fear or Just An Hour stalk and quicken
scenarios.body: Tai Hang Pegasus's moderate front-running on good-to-firm allows the race to develop into a test of sustained speed from the home turn, suiting those who have been travelling smoothly within the first two; Cape Fear's excellent consistent record at this trip and going (sim-going 8/8) makes this the dominant scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get In
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus goes quicker than expected early and the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up horses into play
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop would string the field out and leave the prominent stalkers over-committed, allowing Raulin or Melek Alreeh to pick up past fading leaders in the straight; Raulin's last-time-out win at 12f on good ground and strong similar-going record (11/15, 4W) makes this the most credible closer threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus buries the field early and the stalkers fail to quicken off the bridle
scenarios.body: An unusually dominant display from Tai Hang Pegasus combined with a slow pace that lulls chasers into a false sense of security could see the leader sprint clear before rivals react; the good-to-firm surface and Windsor's undulating finish do not typically favour a lone front-runner holding on, but the tactical frailty of the chasing pack makes this non-trivial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle Up
scenarios.trigger: If the race is muddling and Percival or Morcar navigate traffic to produce a late run
scenarios.body: Both Percival and Morcar are true hold-up types mapped to midfield due to the field's composition, meaning they race out of their natural role and must thread through horses late; their style-fit discount and limited recent form on the turf in this going (Percival sim-going 2/5, Morcar trending over shorter trips) makes this the least likely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Cape Fear is the horse to watch structurally — Oisin Murphy riding a 8/8 similar-going record in the dominant pace shape is as close to a profile match as this race offers, and Andrew Balding's yard is in strong form (T14: 11/70).

Tai Hang Pegasus goes out alone in front but carries a STYLE_FIT flag — if Paddy Bradley is pushed forward to lead against the horse's natural inclinations, watch for it to tire in the final furlong and open the race up for stalkers.

Raulin's 68 days off the track is the key unknown — the hold-up profile is perfect if the pace is genuine, but a ring-rusty reappearance at this trip could see the finishing run come too late or lack its usual sharpness.

Just An Hour ran only 14 days ago and faces a quick turnaround, but Rod Millman's trainer strike rate (T14: 2/23) suggests this could be a horse simply being kept ticking over rather than targeted at this specific race — note whether Lewis Edmunds rides with positive intent or settles conservatively.

Morcar and Percival are both mapped out of their natural hold-up positions — if the race pans out in a muddled fashion with no clear tempo, both could find themselves squeezed between true mid-runners and making their challenge from an awkward position, rather than the wide-open late delivery they need.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator from John Ryan's yard who has finished no better than third in six starts, with a poor recent sim-going record (0 wins from 13) suggesting the Good To Firm conditions here are not the stumbling block but consistency clearly is; Jack Mitchell rides a horse that needs the pace to be genuine to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Ecclefechan returns on a fair 17-day break with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, and a top rating of 69 marks him as the one to beat in this six-runner affair; third last time out is his best recent effort, and although winless in his last six starts, he looks the class angle here from stall 5 off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Boom
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 11/70 14-day strike rate is a significant positive, and Oisin Murphy's involvement upgrades this horse sharply; a genuine hold-up type with one win and two places at 7-8f on Good ground, she needs a fast enough pace to close into — not guaranteed in a field led by a solo front-runner.|
runners_data.comment: Berkshire Boom arrives on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 66 ranks him second of the six, pointing to a live each-way threat despite a lengthy winless run in recent starts — the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Sup Of Red
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's runner has strong hold-up instincts — a natural rear-of-field horse — but the map places it in midfield because the backmarker slots are saturated in this six-runner field; its STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 flags that racing out of its comfort zone tempers its chance, and its sim-going record on similar surfaces (0W1P from 14) is modest.|
runners_data.comment: Placed three starts back and again five starts back, Sup Of Red brings solid placed form to this contest and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with 132 lb from stall 3 to shoulder; the risk is that she has been winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a mare with an excellent recent profile: two wins and five places at 8f, with a win and two seconds in her last three outings including on Good ground; as a prominent racer she is ideally positioned to track Who Is Alice and pounce in the straight, and Ollie Sangster's 2/21 14-day record is acceptable.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and with a speed rating of 58 below her official mark, Buckland Belle is hard to fancy on ratings, though she returns in fair order 19 days after a third last time out, has experience of today's distance and going, and her record includes two wins in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Torbados
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's gelding holds up a solid prominent racing profile and wears a hood, which can sharpen focus; his best effort was a 2nd at 8f on Good going, and Rob Hornby gives him tactical options racing just off the pace, though a winless record since that run and multiple poor finishes need explaining away.|
runners_data.comment: Torbados has run over today's trip and going before and, second last time out, arrives here in decent nick on a 14-day turnaround carrying 130 lb from stall six; the concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter, she will lead from the break on what figures to be an uncontested basis — 47 days off the track is a consideration but the hood (headgear) suggests trainer Grace Harris expects her to be forward enough; her 1m trip debut in a race dominated so far by 6f form is a genuine stamina question that will only be answered in the home straight.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Who Is Alice faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and drawn stall one, carrying 129 lb off an official mark of 57.

races.paceDynamic: Who Is Alice is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, she should dictate from the outset at a tempo of her own choosing — Good To Firm conditions at Windsor over a mile will reward a horse that can control fractions without being pressured. Buckland Belle and Torbados will push forward into prominent positions just off the pace, giving the race a clean, strung-out shape rather than a bunched, tactical one. The hold-up quartet is in reality reduced to Ecclefechan and Berkshire Boom as genuine closers, since Sup Of Red is a true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded — its ability to find its natural position is compromised in this configuration. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently, particularly those with the stamina to sustain a steady honest gallop over a mile on quick ground rather than those relying on a late, compressed finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent pair travel sweetly within range.
scenarios.body: Who Is Alice sets fractions that suit Buckland Belle and Torbados tracking in second and third, with the tempo never fast enough to string the closers into contention off their natural pace; Buckland Belle's strong record of placing at 8f on Good ground and Torbados's recent prominent runs make them ideal beneficiaries of this orderly shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice sets an unsustainably slow tempo and the race explodes in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A crawl would compress the field and create a sprint finish from two out, allowing Berkshire Boom to deploy Oisin Murphy's tactical intelligence for a late surge; Berkshire Boom's 2nd at 7f on Good going and strong trainer form (11/70 over 14 days) make it the likeliest beneficiary of a bunched climax.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are faster than expected and Who Is Alice burns off her prominent shadows.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop would stretch the field and bring genuine closers into play late, but this scenario is materially undermined by Sup Of Red being out of its natural position and unlikely to produce a true hold-up finish; Ecclefechan, who has the most honest hold-up profile of the rear runners, is the most plausible beneficiary but has struggled to convert on similar going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice's long lay-off (47 days) has freshened her and she simply outstays a modest field from the front.
scenarios.body: Having controlled the race from flagfall with no pressure, she could find the reserves to hold on if the pace is truly modest and her rivals fail to accelerate; headgear (hood) and Grace Harris's 3/17 14-day trainer strike rate add a small but real possibility she arrives cherry-ripe.

watchPoints.text: Who Is Alice's stamina is the race's central unknown — if she weakens sharply entering the straight having led throughout, Buckland Belle and Torbados are poised immediately behind and will inherit the race instantly.

Berkshire Boom with Oisin Murphy is significantly eye-catching from a market perspective — watch for significant support that could indicate stable confidence, as the jockey booking alone lifts this runner's claims in a closing scenario.

Sup Of Red is unlikely to get its natural hold-up position in a small field; if it is forced to race more prominently than preferred, its pace figures should be discounted and it may fail to reproduce its best form.

Windsor's mile track is a flat, right-handed oval where a solo front-runner that settles kindly can be very hard to peg back — if Who Is Alice jumps well and establishes a comfortable lead within the first furlong, early race shape will be set in stone.

Good To Firm conditions (confirmed by the going report for both 1m races on the card) favour horses with clean, fluent strides rather than those who relish cut — all six runners are rated OK for the going but Buckland Belle's multiple wins and places on Good ground stand out as a concrete positive.

races.name: Matchbook Loves Racing Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hellcat
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with five of his last eight runs on similar going, placing twice; dropped to a competitive 6f sprint having shaped better over this trip than the form figures suggest, but the 48-day absence and a trainer in modest form (0/9 over 14 days) are negatives.
runners_data.comment: Hellcat has been winless in her last five starts and ranks last on our figures here, making her hard to fancy at face value; a third three starts back offers slim encouragement, but the 48-day absence adds another question mark despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: Has never won in six starts and shows 0W0P on Good-equivalent going in eight attempts; hold-up style over a trip that looked too short last time, and the step back to 6f from 7f-8f runs is a concern for a horse without a clear turn of foot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Angel Summer makes for a difficult proposition, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Magic Lady Mae
runners_data.note: Trainer Mullaney has one winner in five runs over 14 days, and she has a peak headgear entry; her natural running style is hold-up, but the field's composition means she is unlikely to settle as deep as she wants — racing out of role will likely blunt her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Magic Lady Mae does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and 16 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh, though a mark of 50 and a midfield ranking leave her facing a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Two wins from seven runs on Good going and a recent course win over 6f gives her the best current form credentials of the prominent group; the 10-day turnaround is fine given that Fenton has had recent success, and her front-foot style suits if she avoids the early jostle for position.
runners_data.comment: Molly Mac arrives here in career-best form, winning on each of her last two starts and looking a filly in fine fettle off just a ten-day turnaround; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 135 lb from stall six is the chief impost to overcome.

runners_data.name: Star Obsession
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 194-day absence is the biggest red flag — she has never raced over 6f or on turf (all starts on Tapeta, all over 7f-8f), and while Tom Marquand takes the ride, the drop in trip and switch to turf are significant unknowns; she is the lone genuine front-runner, which gives her a tactical edge if fit.
runners_data.comment: Star Obsession has a speed rating of 66 and her rating of 65 marks her out as a genuine threat in this field, yet the 194-day absence is the obvious concern for a filly yet to score in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Venetian Romance
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in seven Good-going starts but is 0W in seven, and last won over 7f rather than this sharp 6f; the hold-up style suits the scenario where pace is hot, but the headgear and the 55-day absence need to be watched alongside Attwater's quiet recent 14-day record (0/11).
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 133 lb from stall 3, Venetian Romance shaped with real promise when second last time out and has experience over today's trip and going; the main risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Cape Toronada
runners_data.note: Two wins from seven runs over 6f on Good going and a 2W3P record in nine similar-going starts makes him the most course-and-distance consistent runner in the field; Rossa Ryan is an upgrade in the saddle and Carroll has had recent success (1/21 over 14 days), though Carroll runners can be in-and-out in these grades.
runners_data.comment: Cape Toronada returns a winner last time out, and was a winner three starts back too, giving her a lively recent profile; however, a trainer strike-rate of just 5% over the last 14 days is a concern, and she carries 133 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed four times in thirteen similar-going starts without winning; recent form of 275746 shows a horse that consistently runs into a place position without landing the blow, and the 11-day turnaround with Michael Bell's yard in steady form makes him a place contender rather than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Koffee And Kale catches the eye on our rating, ranked second in the field, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, so the surface should hold no surprises; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with a second six back his best recent effort.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has shown ability over 6f on Good ground (2/6f/GOO in recent history), but is winless in fifteen similar-going attempts; the 11-day return is manageable, yet the prominent style in a crowded early section means she risks losing her position before the race begins to matter.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Beach Partee finished eighth last time out and ranks seventh of nine on our figures, making him hard to fancy here despite the experience of today's trip and going conditions and a return after just 11 days.

races.paceDynamic: Star Obsession is the sole confirmed front-runner and, dropping back to 6f for the first time after three starts over 7f-8f on Tapeta, will likely bowl along in front unchallenged by any genuine leader — the prominent quartet of Molly Mac, Cape Toronada, Koffee And Kale, and Beach Partee will contest the early positions behind her, creating a scrappy battle for the first 2f that risks producing a messy, wide-running affair around the 2-3f mark. That prominent congestion means at least one or two of those four will be checked or shuffled back, which complicates their chances. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically sit at the rear — Magic Lady Mae is a genuine hold-up runner mapped to midfield because the field shape pushes her forward, meaning her natural finisher's profile may not materialise cleanly. This race shape, with one confirmed lead horse setting a sustainable pace and prominent traffic likely to cause interference, most favours horses that can race close to the pace from a clean draw without fighting for position — the prominent runners who secure a clear, uncontested berth early will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Star Obsession leads at a fair but unchallenged gallop and one prominent runner emerges cleanly from early traffic.
scenarios.body: Star Obsession dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, and the best-placed prominent runner — likely Cape Toronada or Molly Mac, both proven over this C&D trip — tracks in second or third before striking early in the final furlong; the clear early pace with a manageable tempo suits horses who can race prominently without burning energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage causes Star Obsession to go faster than she wishes and the tempo becomes genuinely hot.
scenarios.body: A pressured Star Obsession sets a strong early pace that softens up the prominent runners, leaving the race open to a horse who has tracked at midfield; Venetian Romance or Hellcat, able to settle and produce a sustained late run on Good to Firm ground over 6f, would be the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Dominates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner secures a clean second-row position immediately and the pace is true enough to suit a sustained effort.
scenarios.body: Cape Toronada, with the best recent course-and-distance profile in the field (two wins over 6f Good), settles just off a sound Star Obsession gallop and powers through in the final 2f before any hold-up horse can get to them; the Good to Firm ground underfoot rewards his consistent all-speed profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage creates a gap that allows a genuine hold-up horse to thread through late.
scenarios.body: Angel Summer or Hellcat, sitting widest and furthest back, finds a clear run in the final furlong as tiring prominent runners drop away; this scenario demands the pace to be truly hot and gaps to appear — less likely given Magic Lady Mae's redistribution means the true hold-up contingent is thinner than it appears.

watchPoints.text: Star Obsession has never raced on turf or over 6f — watch for her to be slow to stride into rhythm, which could compress the early pace unexpectedly and tighten the prominent group behind her.

Molly Mac, Cape Toronada, Koffee And Kale, and Beach Partee are all prominent types in a nine-runner field — watch the first 2f for bumping, checking, and wide tracking as at least one is forced to give ground early.
Magic Lady Mae is unlikely to get her natural hold-up position given the field shape — if she is pushed further forward than suits her, watch for her to over-race and tie up in the final furlong.

Star Obsession's 194-day layoff for William Haggas — even with Tom Marquand aboard, a long absence combined with two unknowns (turf, 6f) makes her in-running price volatile if she shows signs of rustiness in the early strides.

Good to Firm underfoot at Windsor (confirmed in going report for this race) will sharpen the pace from the outset — watch for the true pace to be stronger than a nine-runner handicap might suggest, which slightly improves the hold-up runners' prospects.

races.name: Windsor Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Bear Of Saints
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed at 5f on Good ground before (3rd most recently); trainer John O'Shea has had no winners from 7 runs in the 14-day window, and 41 days off is a mild query, but the horse's natural style of racing just off the pace suits this controlled shape well.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a runner-up five starts back, The Bear Of Saints arrives here 41 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 64 suggests he is ahead of his official mark — though he remains winless in recent starts and that sequence is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Dragon God
runners_data.note: Strong recent form at 5f on Good ground (1 win, several placings in 9 similar-going runs); a genuine hold-up type who is almost certain to be forced to race closer than his natural rear position allows in this field, which tempers his finish-line punch but means he'll at least have cover early.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, Dragon God arrives fit on 17 days' rest with distance and going experience to call on, but ranked bottom of nine on our figures and saddled with a trainer firing at just 5% recently, he is very hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Em Jay Kay
runners_data.note: Modest recent form string (189080) and no wins or placings from 15 similar-going starts tells a stark story; races from the rear but the data suggests the position won't be his to choose freely here, and his overall form profile makes him the weakest candidate even if he gets a clean run.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures and officially rated just 52, Em Jay Kay has managed only one win in his last six starts, with a string of unplaced efforts since, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going, a quick turnaround from stall one.

runners_data.name: Our Planet
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 65 and carrying 138lbs — the biggest weight burden; a hold-up horse who has produced a couple of 5f Good wins in his history but has posted a string of mid-pack finishes recently, and the big impost is a significant headwind at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Our Planet nonetheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner in this field, and having run over today's trip and going before, conditions hold no fears; the 16-day turnaround looks sharp enough, though he must find a way past his recent string of disappointing efforts.

runners_data.name: Trafalger
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with five place finishes from nine similar-going runs but still looking for a win; Benoit de la Sayette rides and the 31-day break is not a concern, though getting a clean passage when forced wide by the congested rear in this field is the main tactical obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Trafalger has run over today's trip and going, our rating puts him ahead of his official mark and ranks him second of the nine runners, making him a genuine threat despite being winless in recent starts; the absence of a top-three finish in his last three runs is the concern.

runners_data.name: Just Jump
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course-and-distance combination on Good ground and Tony Carroll's yard has a winner in the 14-day window; races from hold-up position but has the tactical pace to sit closer if needed, making this a genuine contender in the dominant scenario regardless of the redistribution effect.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner three starts back, Just Jump arrives here fresh enough on 20 days' rest and with both distance and going experience in his favour — the chief concern is a trainer who has managed just one winner from 21 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Desdemona
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner who will dictate terms completely unchallenged; 63 days off is a fitness question for connections, and a STYLE_FIT flag suggests her chance should be tempered, but structurally she controls the shape of this race entirely and on Good to Firm over 5f that can be exploited.
runners_data.comment: Desdemona won twice in her last six starts but has finished fifth or worse in each of her three most recent outings, and 63 days off the track adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 133 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Darkened Edge
runners_data.note: Two recent wins from 5f starts (including on Good ground) and a strong overall prominent profile across 10 similar-going runs (2W, 8P); Gina Mangan claims and the 40-day break is modest — this horse's profile of sit close and quicken is the textbook fit for the dominant race shape here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures, Darkened Edge faces a stiff ask here, yet back-to-back wins in her last two starts inject genuine momentum, and she has experience of today's trip and going from stall three carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran with no wins but three placings from nine similar-going 5-6f runs; a true hold-up type who will find himself racing out of his natural rearmost position given the congestion of closers, which undermines his chances unless the pace proves genuinely taxing in the final stages.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but showing some promise with a second two runs back, Faustus has run over today's distance and going before and steps in from stall four carrying 129 lb; a rating of 63 offers a small edge over his official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Desdemona is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate at a controlled, sustainable pace from the front on Good to Firm ground over this sharp Windsor 5f. The Bear Of Saints and Darkened Edge are prominent types who will track close behind, creating a small pocket of early pressure but nothing dramatic enough to force a suicidal gallop. With the pace essentially controlled by a single horse, this sets up as a race where those who can sit just off the leader and produce a straightforward kick into the straight — prominent-to-midfield stalkers — are the principal beneficiaries. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can absorb at the rear: Faustus, Dragon God, and Em Jay Kay are genuine closers who are likely forced wider or slightly closer to the pace than their natural role demands, meaning Desdemona's uncontested lead is the dominant structural feature of this race, favouring prominent sit-and-sprint types over true closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Desdemona Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Desdemona gets a clean break and dictates an unchallenged, even gallop, those stalking close behind are best placed.
scenarios.body: Desdemona rolls along at a measured clip, making the prominent-to-midfield runners hunt her down without burning resources early; those sitting a length or two off the pace travel smoothly and are ideally positioned to strike in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace, Hold-Up Flier
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo proves genuinely even and the hold-up horses get an unimpeded run through, a late burst can reach the leaders.
scenarios.body: Dragon God or Just Jump, operating slightly closer than ideal but with tactical speed to spare, finds a gap in the final 150 yards; the steady fractions mean the winning margin is small and the field compresses late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Desdemona is allowed to set a particularly gentle early clip and the field is slow to respond, she could have enough in reserve to last home.
scenarios.body: Desdemona's connections accept the gift of a soft lead and she builds a two-length advantage entering the final furlong; with the stalkers only arriving late, her fitness edge from a 63-day break is the key uncertainty.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Chaos, Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If a poor start or wide-draw traffic scrambles the predicted pace map and multiple horses contest the early lead.
scenarios.body: The race shape dissolves into a more contested affair as handlers push for position, lifting fractions and suiting any genuine closer who can find a run on the outside.

watchPoints.text: Darkened Edge has won twice on Good-to-Firm ground over 5f in recent starts and races in the exact style this pace map rewards — watch whether Gina Mangan can slot in directly behind Desdemona from the off.

Desdemona's 63-day absence is the single biggest fitness unknown — if she ties up inside the final furlong after controlling the pace, the entire race shape collapses and prominent trackers benefit the most.

Dragon God, Just Jump, Faustus, and Em Jay Kay are all genuine hold-up types competing for the same rear slots; watch for early crowding or erratic traffic as at least two of them are forced to race wider or closer than they want.

Our Planet carries the top weight of 138lbs — monitor whether Callum Shepherd compensates by positioning closer to the pace than usual, as a hold-up horse lugging that weight over 5f on fast ground is unlikely to finish through.

Tom Marquand on Dragon God is worth tracking in-running: if he gets a clean passage and the pace is genuinely honest, Dragon God's course-and-distance winning form on Good ground means he could arrive late with more momentum than his starting position suggests.
